title: Returned Transfers, Dormancy and Reactivation of Payout Methods
content:
A Payout Methods method stops receiving money when a transfer to it comes back or when it goes dormant, and it receives money again only after it is reactivated on re-verified details.

## Terms in force

**R1 — A returned transfer.** When a transfer is returned, its amount comes back to the undisbursed balance and the method is placed on hold with the hold cause "returned payout".

**R2 — Dormancy.** An active method with no transfer for the rail's dormancy period in calendar days (365 days on Direct Deposit (ACH), Fast Pay Debit Card, PayPal and Payoneer; 180 days on International Wire Transfer and Western Union Cash Pickup) is placed on hold with the hold cause "dormant".

**R3 — A method on hold.** A method on hold receives nothing; releases due to it go to the default method, or wait in its balance when it is itself the default.

**R4 — Reactivation.** A method on hold is reactivated only after the host has updated and re-verified its details, shown by a verification date later than the date the method was placed on hold. The method's own record is the evidence; the host's statement that the details were updated is not.

### R4 in cases (hypothetical dates)

| Placed on hold | Verification date on the method record | Reactivation |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-02-12 | 2026-02-15 | Allowed: verified after the hold date |
| 2026-02-12 | 2026-02-12 | Not allowed: not later than the hold date |
| 2026-02-12 | 2025-09-30 (the original verification) | Not allowed: no re-verification since the hold |

### R3 in cases

| The method on hold is | A release due to it goes to |
|---|---|
| Not the default | The default method |
| Itself the default | Waits in its own balance |

## Clauses no longer in force

The following clauses are **no longer in force**; each has been superseded by the current basis the company applies to the matter it covered:

- *"The rail's returned-payout fee (where above 0.00) is charged once as a returned-payout fee."* No longer in force; the charge on a returned transfer follows the current basis for return charges.
- *"On reactivation the held balance is transferred at the next run."* No longer in force; what becomes of a reactivated method's held balance follows the current basis for re-sending it.

superseded_clauses: the rail's returned_payout_fee_usd (where above 0.00) is charged once as a returned_payout_fee
On reactivation the held balance is transferred at the next run.
